$comment: Dependencies this repository deliberately replaced with first-party code,
and the mechanical ban that keeps each one out. One declaration, one
contract test, rather than a bespoke assertion per retirement.
WHY A LEDGER RATHER THAN MORE ASSERTIONS. The same argument
config/derivations.json makes about stale artifacts. Retirements here were
enforced three different ways and mostly not at all: turndown had two lines
inside a test about something else, exiftool and jq had prose in
config/tools.json and in CLAUDE.md, and nothing anywhere stopped any of
them coming back. A retirement that is only written down is a preference.
Adding one here is a data edit and the check is already written.
THE BANS LAND ON DECLARATION FILES, NEVER ON FREE TEXT, and that is forced
rather than tidy. Every retired name still appears in this tree on purpose,
because the comment recording a retirement has to name the thing it
retired: extract-photo-metadata.sh says `BOTH NAMES BELOW ARE jq ON PURPOSE,
because they are history`. A scanner over text would fire on exactly the
prose that documents the decision, which is the trap CLAUDE.md's own note
about path rewrites describes from the other side. So a ban asks the file a
dependency would have to be re-added to for it to work at all: a package.json
dependency map, config/tools.json's `bin`, a Cargo.toml dependency or
feature, or an anchored import statement in source.
WHAT `npm` CANNOT SEE, stated because the gap is silent. It reads the four
dependency maps of every committed package.json and never bun.lock, so a
retired package arriving as somebody else's transitive stays invisible.
That is deliberate: @cloudflare/workers-types is an OPTIONAL PEER of
wrangler and sits in bun.lock today, so a lockfile ban would fail on a tree
that is correct. The claim a ban makes is `this repo does not ask for it`,
which is the claim that stops it being used.
SCOPE IS PART OF THE RECORD. `Pillow` is retired from the photo pipeline
and still serves one page generator, so its entry names that file as an
exception rather than claiming a clean kill. A ledger that rounded that to
`retired` would be wrong in the direction nobody checks.
WHEN TO REPLACE A DEPENDENCY WITH CODE. Commonware's rule is `implement
core mechanisms and algorithms inside the workspace rather than adding a
dependency for them`, and every entry below already passed some version of
that test. Written out, what this repo has actually required:
1. THE REPLACEMENT IS MEASURED AGAINST THE DEPENDENCY, on the axis that
motivated it, before the dependency leaves. Every `measured` field below
is a number somebody took. A swap with no number is a preference wearing
a commit message.
2. OUTPUT DOES NOT MOVE, or moving it is the point and is priced. `/a/` and
`/i/` are content-addressed, so one changed byte remints URLs and
orphans every dictionary and histogram derived from them. zenjpeg's
`parallel` feature was droppable because 6 of 6 thumbnails and 4 of 4
archives came back byte-identical; the avifenc `--speed` change was
worth 495 reminted URLs and said so up front.
3. THE SURFACE IS SMALLER THAN THE DEPENDENCY. zenc is one encoder call
this repo controls, against a from-source libjxl build. A first-party
replacement that reimplements the whole library is a fork, and a fork is
a dependency with worse support.
4. THE DEPENDENCY WAS COSTING SOMETHING ONGOING, in maintenance, bytes, or
attention. @cloudflare/workers-types spent 12 of 29 dependabot pull
requests in one month describing a runtime this repo does not run on.
A quiet dependency that does its job is not a candidate.
5. IT DOES NOT ADD AN INTERPRETER OR A TOOLCHAIN. The histogram bake moving
into zenc removed python3 and pip from the core pipeline, which is worth
more than the milliseconds it also saved.
THE COUNTER-RULE, because four of the entries below are swaps rather than
in-house builds. Readability replaced Defuddle and jaq replaced jq, both
third-party. Prefer the dependency when the thing it does is a standard
somebody else conforms to and drift from it is the actual risk. Writing a
third HTML-to-Markdown extractor would make /lens's premise weaker rather
than stronger, since that surface exists to show what a WIDELY DEPLOYED
extractor discards.

retired.replaced_by: lens-reader/src/reader.ts, a first-party Markdown walk over Readability's own node
retired.why: A general HTML-to-Markdown dependency restores a second traversal and a tree clone: the old path serialized Readability's article node, reparsed that HTML into a third linkedom document, and handed the reconstruction to the converter. It also shipped two builds, and wrangler resolved the wrong one.
retired.measured: Its browser build reaches for document.implementation.createHTMLDocument, so turndown(htmlString) threw `document is not defined` inside a Worker while passing under node --test. Measured both ways 2026-08-10. The node build falls back to @mixmark-io/domino and hides it.

retired.why: A swap rather than an in-house build, and deliberately so: /lens's seventh tab exists to report what a WIDELY DEPLOYED extractor discards, and Readability is the one behind Firefox Reader View. Defuddle keeps <button> text on purpose, which is the failure tools/lib/html-to-md.ts rule 2 exists to refuse.
retired.measured: 11.4 KB gzip against 90.0, taking the Reader Worker from 237.68 to 153.17 KB. On /garage/horizon it leaks 3 of 26 control labels as prose where Defuddle leaked 14. Not uniformly better: on stripe.com it leaks 5 where Defuddle leaked 2, which is why the `controls` readout stays on the payload.

retired.why: cal was the last consumer, and @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers dragged a second test runner plus its own miniflare floor into a tree whose every other suite is bun:test or node --test. The harness reaches local KV and Workflow bindings through wrangler's createTestHarness() instead.
retired.measured: The harness boots cal in 142ms under bun against 269ms under node, returns all 17 bindings and vars, round-trips a KV put/get/list, and hands back a live Workflow introspector. Its mockEvent and forceEventTimeout are read from wrangler's types and NOT exercised, so treat those two as unproven under bun.

retired.replaced_by: config/.generated/, written by tools/gen-runtime-types.ts from the pinned workerd
retired.why: The package describes a runtime version of its own choosing, and this repo pins workerd exactly. Generating from the pinned binary makes the types a function of what actually runs, and the cache key is wrangler's version plus the config bytes, so it costs 3s cold and 0.02s warm.
retired.measured: 12 of 29 dependabot pull requests in one month were bumps to this package, for a runtime this repo did not run on.

retired.replaced_by: addScriptTag on the existing env.BROWSER Quick Action, with the allowlist in src/worker/lens-recipes.ts
retired.why: Never adopted. A live CDP session counts against the free plan's 3 concurrent browsers and 1-new-instance-per-20-seconds, which Quick Actions do not, so a public unauthenticated session would black out /lens/shot and /lens/browser. Holding one also needs a new Durable Object class plus a [[migrations]] entry, which `wrangler versions upload` is refused for by the API (error 10211).
retired.measured: ~1 MB of ESM against a Worker bundle already over its 204.24 KiB gzip budget. What shipped instead is one query parameter, no new route, no new binding, and no dependency.

retired.why: Its --keyed mode emits metadata.json's record shape and the Fujifilm recipe card directly, and --merge-into owns the merge. That retired a 50-line jq reshape, build-recipes.py, and the last Python on that script's path. The merge is the reason more than the speed: jq's `*` is recursive and the reflexive substitute `+` is shallow, which drops the recipe card from every re-merged photo in silence.
retired.measured: Regenerating all 158 committed photos produced records byte-identical to what exiftool + jq + Python produced, recipe cards included. 9.9ms against exiftool's 995ms over the same 160 files. Do not chase the speed further: 9.6ms of that is the I/O floor for opening those files.

retired.why: A swap rather than an in-house build. The per-stem split still wants a jq-language interpreter, and jaq is the faster implementation of the same language. One real incompatibility, worth knowing before reaching back: jaq does not slurp ACROSS MULTIPLE FILE ARGUMENTS, so `jaq -s` over two files processes each separately where jq builds one array of 2. Nothing here uses -s.
retired.measured: Every remaining filter diffed engine against engine over the real 165-photo library and matched byte for byte: --slurpfile, -S, --arg, -n, with_entries, has, to_entries, array subtraction, and the photo-index merge.

retired.why: cjpegli meant a from-source libjxl build in the photo pipeline's path. zenc is one crate this repo controls, with hybrid trellis plus a 64-candidate progressive scan search and sharp_yuv chroma, and dependabot tracks the zenjpeg pin.
retired.measured: ~4% under cjpegli at equal quality. q84 on zenc is roughly the old cjpegli q82.

retired.why: The feature was carried on the claim that it speeds the 2000px square inputs, which was never a number. zenc's own source never touches rayon; the feature only reaches zenjpeg's internals, which is why it buys so little on images this size.
retired.measured: +2.7% on the 600px thumbnail tier (+1.5 ms/photo over 9 alternating trials) and +1.1% on the 2000px archive, for SIX crates and 194,704 bytes of binary, 10.8% of it. Safe to drop because output did not move: byte-identical on 6 of 6 thumbnails and 4 of 4 archives. Re-add it only with a measurement on the tier that motivates it, and check byte-identity in the same run.

retired.replaced_by: `zenc histogram`, which bakes the four 64-bin RGB and luminance channels inside the encoder crate
retired.why: A SCOPED retirement, recorded as one rather than rounded to a clean kill. Neither add-photos.sh nor extract-photo-metadata.sh needs Pillow any more, so the core pipeline no longer needs python3 plus a venv, which matters because Homebrew's python3 is PEP 668 externally managed and refuses `pip install` outright. tools/photos/gen-pixel-peeper.py still uses it and is a one-off page generator rather than part of any pipeline.
retired.measured: A missing Pillow now costs one study page's regeneration rather than the histograms on 158 photos.
